source.title: Statistical Measures For Defining Curriculum Scoring Function

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether changing training-example ordering through curriculum learning affects test performance, using methods different from the claim versions' interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for statistical and dynamic curricula. It does not test random-label memorization or any listed version. Mentioned optimizer comparisons are cited prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study's separate CNN-8 and FCN-512 results on CIFAR-10 bear on V3: Figure 4 places CNN accuracy around 79% and FCN accuracy around 49.4%. Both are trained with SGD. This is a cross-case architecture comparison, without isolating local connectivity; the curriculum interventions themselves test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that statistical curricula improve image-classification performance, including noisy-label settings, and that within-epoch ordering and curriculum tuning matter. Their dynamic curriculum is an analytical, computationally expensive method requiring a reference solution obtained through prior vanilla training.
record.recipe_differences: Uses curriculum-based example ordering and dynamic curriculum sampling, rather than the interventions specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on curriculum variant and dataset; DCL+ generalization depends on tuning pacing parameter k, with k = 0.6 best among the tested values in Figure 8.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard-deviation curricula improve mean test accuracy by approximately 1.05 percentage points across nine cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dataset-appropriate standard-deviation curricula can improve image-classification accuracy over vanilla sampling.

fits_no_version.finding: DCL+ reaches vanilla performance milestones earlier; ordering and pacing affect its results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic curriculum sampling can change convergence speed and held-out performance, depending on ordering and pacing.

fits_no_version.finding: First-epoch correlations between standard deviation and the curriculum gradient-alignment score are 0.74 and 0.36.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image standard deviation is associated with the dynamic curriculum score early in training.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report useful curriculum performance with 20% label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Statistical curricula can improve performance in the tested partially corrupted-label settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on SubSetML: Subset Selection in Machine Learning: From Theory to Practice at the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning
record.problems: No random-label or memorization-capacity test. Main accuracy comparisons are summarized as an aggregate mean improvement; case-level values are shown in figures without exact values in the text. Dynamic-curriculum experiments are limited to small datasets; k is tuned by trial and error, with fine-tuning based on training accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure-only case-level accuracy values and most Figure 8 values are not reconstructed from plots.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.

The contribution of local connectivity, learning sparse local connections, and initialization from a trained convolutional network. Fashion-MNIST architecture differences cannot be resolved reliably from the supplied figure text.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD performance; the introduction cites prior work but reports no optimizer comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Effects of adding or removing dropout. Dropout appears in the CNN recipe without an ablation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing examples selected by label-memorization influence versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Separate CIFAR-10 architecture results: CNN-8 in Case 2 achieves approximately 79% accuracy, whereas FCN-512 in Case 8 achieves approximately 49.4%. Record architecture and sampling condition separately; exact bar values are unavailable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks the architecture comparison available across CIFAR-10 cases. Figure-only case values were declared untranscribed, but the missing issue is their relevance to V3. The supplied figure text establishes a large accuracy separation without supporting exact individual bar values. The paper also inconsistently describes Case 9 as ResNet-20 in Section 3.2 and CNN-8 in Supplement B.1.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test performance.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on matched settings as the version specifies.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.
No dropout intervention or comparison of removing dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of generalization-gap rankings.

rows.subject: CNN-8, FCN-512, and ResNet-20 models across Cases 1–9 (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: CNN-8: 8 convolution layers and 2 fully-connected layers; FCN-512: 2-layer fully-connected network with 512 hidden neurons; ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Train with standard-deviation curriculum rather than vanilla sampling; aggregate reported across nine test cases.

conditions.value: Small Mammals, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet Cats, Fashion-MNIST, and MNIST
25 independent trials for Cases 2, 3, 5–8; 10 independent trials for Cases 1, 4, 9

rows.baseline: vanilla; exact accuracy values not stated in text
rows.value: mean improvement of ∼ 1.05% top-1 test accuracy
rows.note: Aggregate statement across test cases; individual case values are presented in figures without recoverable exact numbers in the text.
rows.check: The aggregate curriculum improvement does not measure any listed version. Architecture-specific results must be separated to assess V3.

rows.subject: FCN-10
rows.operation_detail: Compare DCL+ with vanilla SGD on the binary MNIST subset; compare test loss over training steps.

conditions.value: subset of MNIST with class labels 0 and 1

rows.measure: Training step at which DCL+ reaches vanilla's final test loss
rows.baseline: vanilla final test loss at training step 1000
rows.value: DCL+ reaches that score at training step 682
rows.note: The authors state all networks achieve the same test accuracy.
rows.check: Correctly reports a curriculum convergence milestone, which measures none of the listed versions.

rows.subject: FCN-128
rows.operation_detail: Compare DCL+ with vanilla SGD on Small Mammals; compare test accuracy over training steps.
rows.measure: Training step at which DCL+ reaches vanilla's convergence test-accuracy score
rows.baseline: vanilla convergence test-accuracy score at training step 4900
rows.value: DCL+ reaches that score at training step 1896
rows.note: The paper says DCL+ achieves faster and better convergence than vanilla in this experiment.
rows.check: Correctly reports a curriculum convergence milestone, which measures none of the listed versions.

rows.subject: FCN-10
rows.operation_detail: Compare DCL+ and DCL−, which expose the same examples in each epoch in opposite order.

conditions.value: subset of MNIST with class labels 0 and 1

rows.value: DCL− has high discontinuities in the test-loss curve after every epoch; DCL+ shows the fastest convergence
rows.note: Qualitative comparison; the paper argues that within-epoch mini-batch ordering matters.
rows.check: Within-epoch ordering and test-loss discontinuities do not measure a listed version; partial is therefore inappropriate.

rows.subject: FCN-128
rows.operation_detail: Compare DCL+ and DCL−, which expose the same examples in each epoch in opposite order.
rows.value: DCL+ achieves faster and better convergence than vanilla; text gives no separate numerical DCL− comparison
rows.note: The explicit ordering conclusion refers to Figure 7, but the text does not specify a separate DCL− outcome for this experiment.
rows.check: The stated value compares DCL+ with vanilla, whereas the operation and baseline specify DCL+ versus DCL−. It duplicates R3 rather than recording a separate ordering result.

rows.subject: FCN-10
rows.operation_detail: Measure correlation between example standard deviation and ρ values after the first epoch.
rows.measure: Correlation between ρ and standard deviation
rows.note: This correlation is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
rows.check: The reported correlation concerns image statistics and gradient alignment, not magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap ranking.

rows.subject: FCN-128
rows.operation_detail: Measure correlation between example standard deviation and ρ values after the first epoch.
rows.measure: Correlation between ρ and standard deviation
rows.note: This correlation is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
rows.check: The reported correlation concerns image statistics and gradient alignment, not magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap ranking.

rows.subject: CNN-8
rows.operation_detail: Apply standard-deviation curriculum in experiments with noisy labels.
rows.value: The authors state that the curriculum algorithms work well in these settings; exact values are figure-only.
rows.note: The paper says curriculum hyperparameters received only coarse fine-tuning for these experiments.
rows.check: Training with 20% label noise does not establish V1's random-label fit and chance-level held-out performance. Figure 5 specifies 25 CIFAR-100 trials and 10 ImageNet Cats trials, contrary to trials being unstated.

rows.subject: FCN-128
rows.operation_detail: Vary the DCL+ pacing fraction k.
rows.measure: Top-1 test accuracy across pacing fractions
rows.value: A moderate k = 0.6 generalizes the best; other exact values are figure-only.
rows.note: The paper says k needs to be finely tuned; the comparison supports the curriculum result but is not a mapped claim version.
rows.check: Curriculum pacing is neither network width nor batch size and measures none of the listed versions.

relationships.condition: CNN-8 versus FCN-512 on CIFAR-10, across the separately reported training cases.
relationships.reason: Based on text omitted from the rows: Figure 4(b,h) shows approximately 79% CNN accuracy versus 49.4% FCN accuracy. This supports the architecture performance difference, without identifying its cause.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher CNN-8 test accuracy remains unverified across the separately configured training cases.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
